main_text.l: Suavis apis cursu Is, nam currit ut optima fingat

l.i: Perge ita: sic clarus rutilis evadere squamis
Mox poteris, gravidas ut Maro laudat apes.

main_text.l: εἰς φιλίας πεχμήςλον P.Joh. Conradus Heideggerus,S. Theolog. Cand.

Terras jam dudum ferro populatur & igniBellipotens Mavors, cristata cassride cinctus;Quaque patet tellus vitreo circumsona PontoClassica saeva tonant, Taratantara dira cientur,Horridus exigitur per viscera saucia mucro,Luctus ubique, nigrae & quam plurima mortis imago est.Gradivus tremulum vaecors sic concutit orbem.Haud multum pugna est Bellonā mitior istā,Ad quam conclamat lituisque tubāque crepanteEffrons turba Sophūm, cui mens & cornea fibra est,Haud equidem heic fuso pinguescunt sanguine campi;Haud Martis pulli portant in bella bipennes,Loricam haud miles ventri succingit atrocem,Haudque Thraso creperus sua spicula lucida tergitArvinā pingui, nec manant stagna cruore.Alter in alterius sed rumpit nomen habenisLaxatis mordax, non hospes ab hospite tutus.Figere discipulus Doctori tentat ocellum,Et placita inflectit tyro veneranda Magistri.Indus, Arabs, Syrus, ac Theuton, recutitus apellaHoc pallent morbo, hac sudant praecordia culpā.

page.notes: The Greek line in the dedication is printed in a small italic hand and is transcribed as legibly as possible; the final lines of the poem are partly obscured by show-through, so some letters, notably in "Sophūm" and "recutitus", may be doubtful. Lines of the poem are printed as verse lines and are given as continuous text within one paragraph for the stanza.
